records.title: Decoding cancer therapy resistance through advanced 3D organoid systems.
records.abstract: Precision oncology still faces low clinical translation rates. This is largely because two-dimensional (2D) culture systems cannot reproduce tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stress. Here, we review the applications of 3D cancer models, including scaffold-free spheroids, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) biobanks, and microphysiological systems (MPSs), in drug resistance modeling and personalized therapy. These platforms effectively model metabolic gradients, lineage plasticity, and immunological features within the tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby bridging the genotype-phenotype gap. They also capture physical immune exclusion, T cell exhaustion, and antigen presentation to facilitate the evaluation of immunotherapies. Last, we discuss key translational bottlenecks such as standardization and throughput, proposing the integration of advanced biomanufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenomics, and computational modeling to develop 3D cancer platforms into clinical predictive systems for optimizing precision treatment strategies.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted discovery of natural product geroprotectors: target prediction, aging biomarker identification, and drug repurposing.
records.abstract: Natural products derived from traditional medicines are valuable sources of potential geroprotective compounds; however, their translation into therapeutic candidates is limited by chemical complexity, polypharmacology, limited mechanistic resolution, and lengthy experimental validation. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers an emerging framework for integrating chemical, pharmacological, multi-omics, imaging, and literature derived data to accelerate natural product anti-aging research. This review summarizes recent applications of AI in three interconnected areas: drug repurposing, prediction of aging-related targets and signaling pathways, and identification of biomarkers for biological aging and cellular senescence. AI integrates chemical, molecular, omics, and imaging data to prioritize candidate compounds, predict drug-target interactions, identify synergistic combinations, and reveal mechanisms underlying geroprotection. However, computational predictions should not be interpreted as evidence of efficacy or causality. Data heterogeneity, sampling bias, limited model interpretability, inadequate external validation, and insufficient pharmacokinetic and long-term safety assessment remain major barriers to translation. Future progress will require an iterative framework that combines AI prediction with target engagement studies, senescence models, organoids, animal experiments, and clinical biomarker validation. This integrated strategy may improve the efficiency, reproducibility, and translational potential of natural product geroscience research.

records.title: Environmental Microbiomes as Sources of Postbiotic Therapeutics: A One Health Perspective on Translational Applications.
records.abstract: Environmental microbiomes are reservoirs of specialized microorganisms with implications for ecosystem functionality, host health, and therapeutic discovery. Soil, marine, plant-associated, wastewater, freshwater, and extreme-environment microbiomes contain communities capable of producing bioactive metabolites and functional biomolecules. Postbiotics-non-viable microorganisms and their functional components that confer health benefits-offer potential advantages in stability, safety, scalability, and pharmaceutical development. This review examines environmental microbiomes as sources of postbiotic therapeutics within a One Health framework. A critical integrative translational review synthesized literature on environmental microbiomes, postbiotic diversity, molecular mechanisms, therapeutic applications, technological advances, and barriers to clinical translation. Evidence was organized across ecological sources, postbiotic classes, human-health applications, discovery platforms, pharmaceutical development, and translational challenges. Environmental microbiomes represent chemically and functionally diverse reservoirs of postbiotic candidates shaped by ecological adaptation, microbial competition, and environmental selection. Major classes-including short-chain fatty acids, bacteriocins, extracellular vesicles, indole and tryptophan metabolites, exopolysaccharides, and microbial/lytic enzymes-act through receptor signaling, immune modulation, barrier protection, antimicrobial activity, metabolic regulation, intercellular communication, and enzymatic target modification. Metagenomics, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, synthetic biology, organoid and microfluidic models, advanced delivery systems, and biomanufacturing increasingly enable discovery and development. However, reproducibility, microbiome variability, manufacturing scalability, regulatory standardization, cost, and equitable translation remain barriers. Environmental microbiomes provide important reservoirs for postbiotic discovery. Integrating ecological microbiology with multi-omics, computational innovation, pharmaceutical engineering, and human-relevant validation could accelerate development of defined, reproducible, and scalable postbiotic therapeutics. Preserving microbial ecosystem diversity is relevant to environmental sustainability and future microbiome-derived therapeutic innovation within One Health medicine.

records.title: Establishment and characterisation of primary human oesophageal organoids as a versatile epithelial model.
records.abstract: Human patient-derived oesophageal epithelial models are limited, and organoid cultures often have short passaging lifespans, restricting studies of tissue homeostasis and disease. We aimed to establish and characterise primary oesophageal organoids from non-pathologic epithelium as a renewable epithelial source and adaptable modelling platform. Primary oesophageal tissues were obtained from endoscopic biopsies and surgical resections. Basal epithelial cells were isolated and cultured under optimised conditions to establish long-term three-dimensional organoids. Organoid-derived cells were expanded as two-dimensional monolayers and re-seeded into 3D culture. Epithelial identity and differentiation were assessed by immunostaining and RT-qPCR (reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction) analysis of markers. Primary organoids were established and maintained while preserving epithelial markers. Expression of KRT14, involucrin, loricrin and filaggrin confirmed the oesophageal phenotype. Larger, multilayered primary organoids showed increased expression of differentiation-associated markers relative to 2D monolayers and re-seeded small organoids, indicating culture configuration influences epithelial differentiation while maintaining lineage identity. We established a robust and reproducible protocol for generating and maintaining oesophageal organoids across culture formats. These models retained epithelial features while exhibiting culture-dependent differentiation. This platform enables complementary 2D and 3D investigation of oesophageal epithelial biology and supports future comparison of healthy and disease-derived tissues for patient-specific modelling and mechanistic studies.

records.title: Current State and Critical Challenges in Prostate Cancer Organoid Culture.
records.abstract: Three-dimensional prostate cancer organoids represent a promising platform for modeling tumor biology and personalizing therapeutic strategies. However, unlike many other solid tumors, reproducing this pathology in vitro is challenging. Despite initial culture establishment rates reaching 70-90% in certain studies, most cultures undergo early growth arrest (typically within passages P1-P3 or the first 1-2 months), accompanied by a high risk of losing the target tumor clone. In the present work, we provide a critical analysis of the current state of 3D prostate cancer culture technologies and attempt to identify the fundamental reasons for the inefficiency of standard multicomponent media and traditional extracellular matrices. Based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomic profiling data, we characterized the adaptive drift of organoid cellular composition toward basal and transient states. Furthermore, we substantiated the critical need to modernize approaches for confirming model relevance, particularly by analyzing in detail the limitations of traditional markers. As an effective solution, we propose the concept of integrating multiplex expression test systems based on accessible quantitative PCR platforms, utilizing the extensive arsenal of highly informative RNA biomarkers accumulated in clinical urologic oncology. We conclude that the transition from empirical condition selection to directed niche reconstruction based on single-cell analysis data combined with PCR verification will open new opportunities for the widespread implementation of organoid models in basic research and clinical practice.

records.title: Synergistic Cytotoxic Effect of Type 4 Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors and Autophagy Suppressors on Osteosarcoma.
records.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS), the predominant primary malignant bone neoplasm diagnosed in adolescents and young adults, is characterized by poor prognoses upon the development of metastatic disease or tumor recurrence. Bioinformatics analysis indicates that high phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) expression correlates with unfavorable outcomes in OS patients, suggesting PDE4 as a potential therapeutic target. The present investigation was undertaken to evaluate the antineoplastic efficacy of Zl-n-91, a novel PDE4 inhibitor, and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms within preclinical models of osteosarcoma. To assess PDE4's role, we analyzed its expression in the TARGET database. The impacts of Zl-n-91 on OS cell proliferation, cell cycle, apoptosis, and mitochondrial function (via RNA-seq, TEM, and functional assays) were examined in vitro. Autophagy was monitored with fluorescent reporters and inhibited pharmacologically. Finally, therapeutic efficacy and synergy with chloroquine were validated in mouse xenograft and patient-derived organoid models. Zl-n-91 markedly suppressed the proliferation of OS cells via triggering cell cycle arrest at the G2/M or G0/G1 phase and initiating mitochondrial-dependent apoptosis. In vivo, it suppressed xenograft tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, Zl-n-91 induced autophagy and apoptosis via the cAMP-AMPK-ULK1 signaling axis. Critically, the combination of Zl-n-91 with chloroquine (CQ) synergistically suppressed tumor growth in vivo and in PDOs. The synergistic effect observed with autophagy inhibition highlights a promising combinatorial strategy, positioning Zl-n-91 as a potential therapeutic agent for OS treatment. Zln- 91 represents a proprietary, novel inhibitor exhibiting selectivity for PDE4D, with its safety profile firmly established through preclinical evaluation, and this study is the first to report its anti-osteosarcoma activity and synergistic effect with autophagy inhibitors. This work expands the therapeutic indications of this existing patented compound and provides critical preclinical evidence for its new indication patent application and clinical translation in osteosarcoma treatment, which is consistent with the direction of recent patented anti-cancer drug development. By inducing cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction, Zl-n-91 inhibits osteosarcoma progression, and its combination with autophagy inhibition represents a promising therapeutic strategy for OS.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models.
records.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
records.abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

records.title: Protein engineering in Brazil: a biophysical perspective.
records.abstract: Protein engineering has become an increasingly interdisciplinary field, integrating molecular biology, structural biology, biophysics, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence to modify protein structure, stability, dynamics, molecular recognition, and catalytic activity. This systematic review examines the historical development and scientific contributions of protein engineering research associated with Brazilian institutions between 1988 and June 2026. A total of 792 peer-reviewed articles were identified in PubMed through eight thematic search strategies covering protein and enzyme engineering, directed evolution, rational and computational design, recombinant protein expression, therapeutic proteins, structural biology, and artificial intelligence-assisted engineering. The reviewed literature reveals a transition from early residue-level mutagenesis and conventional biochemical assays to increasingly integrated experimental and computational approaches. Advances in X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), circular dichroism (CD), mass spectrometry, small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), calorimetry, molecular dynamics, and structural bioinformatics enabled the quantitative investigation of protein folding, stability, conformational landscapes, molecular interactions, and catalytic mechanisms. More recently, machine learning, protein language models, AlphaFold-derived structures, and generative approaches have expanded the capacity to predict mutations and design proteins, peptides, antibodies, and enzymes with predefined properties. Overall, protein engineering in Brazil has evolved into a mature and diverse field with applications in health, infectious diseases, agriculture, biotechnology, bioenergy, biomaterials, environmental remediation, and industrial biocatalysis. The findings indicate that biophysics has moved beyond a predominantly descriptive role and has become central to the design and validation of engineered proteins. Future progress will depend on the convergence of experimental biophysics, multiscale simulations, artificial intelligence, high-throughput validation, and stronger national and international research networks.

records.title: Evolutionary divergence of uric acid catabolic enzymes: structure-function constraints and genomic innovations across taxa.
records.abstract: Uric acid degradation is a model for understanding how gene duplication, loss, and functional divergence drive metabolic evolution. In hominoids and uricotelic animals, uric acid is the terminal purine catabolite, whereas most other taxa further degrade it to allantoin and beyond. Comparative genomics and structural analyses reveal recurrent duplication and repurposing of key enzymes. 5-Hydroxyisourate hydrolase (HIUase) and transthyretin (TTR) share a common ancestral hydrolase, later diverging through neofunctionalization, while independent gene fusions reshaped the pathway, notably the gene fusion of Urah (HIUase) and Urad (2-oxo-4-hydroxy-4-carboxy-5-ureidoimidazoline decarboxylase, or OHCUd) into single-chain allantoin synthases in plants, diatoms, and bacteria. Elastic network modeling this gene fusion shows uncorrelated motions between the catalytic domains, suggesting its advantage stems from fixed stoichiometry and spatial proximity rather than conformational coupling. Further divergence is seen in enzyme families with complementary substrate specificities, and gene clustering in bacteria and yeast reflects regulatory optimization under nitrogen limitation, paralleling the ureide pathway in legumes. In hominoids, pseudogenization of urate oxidase relaxed constraints on downstream enzymes, elevating serum uric acid, an ancestral adaptation now linked to hyperuricemia. Gut microbiome-mediated degradation and links between Urad variants and cancer risk underscore the pathway's continuing relevance. Mammalian Urad orthologs show strong sequence conservation. Molecular modeling of the human ortholog demonstrated a conserved fold, consistent with a predominantly α-helical secondary structure content supported by circular dichroism, whereas kinetic characterization revealed the absence of detectable catalytic activity. Building on these principles, evolution-guided protein engineering achieved partial functional interconversion between transthyretins and HIUases without disrupting the ancestral scaffold, revealing purine catabolism's plasticity as a model for enzyme innovation and the metabolism-disease-protein design interface.

records.title: PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.
records.abstract: Target-specific 3D molecular generation is a promising approach for structure-based drug design. However, existing diffusion-based methods are generally restricted to marginal distributions with closed-form solutions, limiting the flexibility of generative process design, especially for the forward noising process. As a result, these methods may be less effective in modeling the complex distributions underlying pocket-conditioned molecular generation. We develop Perturbed Flow Matching (PFM), a flow-matching-based framework for protein pocket-conditioned 3D molecular generation. PFM employs a perturbed conditional probability path that incorporates both pocket binding-site information and coupled atom type-coordinate information, enabling more effective generation of molecules in protein binding environments. On CrossDocked2020, PFM achieves competitive structural quality and the best average Vina score among the evaluated unguided methods (-7.12); PFM-G further improves the score to -8.70 with tailored classifier-free guidance. Experiments on additional molecular datasets further confirm the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed framework. https://github.com/kurisu92725/PFM.

records.title: De novo design of miniprotein inhibitors of bacterial adhesins.
records.abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections necessitates the discovery of novel antimicrobial strategies. Here, we show that protein design provides a generalizable means of generating new antimicrobials by neutralizing the function of bacterial adhesins, which are virulence factors critical in host-pathogen interactions. We de novo designed high-affinity miniprotein binders to FimH and Abp chaperone usher pili adhesins from uropathogenic Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii, respectively, which are implicated in mediating both uncomplicated and catheter-associated urinary tract infections (UTI) responsible for significant morbidity worldwide. The designed antagonists have high specificity and stability, disrupt bacterial recognition of host receptors, block biofilm formation, and are effective in treating and preventing murine models of uncomplicated and catheter-associated UTIs in vivo.

records.title: Pharmacophore-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Ligand-Based De Novo Drug Design.
records.abstract: Developing bioactive molecules remains a central, time- and cost-heavy challenge in drug discovery, particularly for novel targets lacking structural or functional data. Pharmacophore modeling presents an alternative for capturing the key features required for molecular bioactivity against a biological target. In this work, we present PharmaDiff, a pharmacophore-conditioned diffusion model for 3D molecular generation. PharmaDiff employs a transformer-based architecture to integrate an atom-based representation of the 3D pharmacophore into the generative process, enabling the precise generation of 3D molecular graphs that align with predefined pharmacophore hypotheses. Through comprehensive testing, PharmaDiff demonstrates superior performance in matching 3D pharmacophore constraints compared to ligand-based drug design methods. Additionally, it achieves higher docking scores across a range of proteins in structure-based drug design, without the need for target protein structures. By integrating pharmacophore modeling with 3D generative techniques, PharmaDiff offers a powerful and flexible framework for rational drug design.

records.title: Intelligent Modular Dual-Readout Architecture Driven by CRISPR/Cas13a-CHA Cascade and Machine Learning for Portable Multiplex MicroRNA Liquid Biopsy in Early Lung Cancer.
records.abstract: Precise detection of trace miRNAs in liquid biopsies is critical for early lung cancer screening, yet current methods are frequently limited by complex reverse transcription procedures and potential enzymatic amplification biases. Herein, we developed a sequencing-free and highly portable dual-mode biosensing platform for decentralized clinical diagnostics by synergizing highly specific CRISPR/Cas13a recognition with exponential non-enzymatic catalytic hairpin assembly amplification (CHA). Trace target miRNAs activate Cas13a to trans-cleave the RNA trigger strand, while intact RNA triggers can precisely initiate downstream assembly networks. The Cas13a molecular lock completely eliminates spontaneous hairpin crosslinking interference. Based on this mechanism, we separately constructed a fluorescence and a multiplex surface-enhanced Raman scattering biosensing platform. The catalytic network drives reporter-embedded bimetallic nanoparticles to specifically bind plasmonic chips, forming sandwich resonance structures for absolute multiplex spectral quantification. The system synchronously processes and analyzes four lung cancer-associated miRNAs within 80 min, achieving an ultralow attomolar diagnostic limit and an exceptionally broad linear dynamic range spanning ten orders of magnitude. Clinical validation using 50 plasma samples demonstrated high quantitative agreement with standard qRT-PCR alongside exceptional anti-interference characteristics. Integrating a machine classification model to extract spectral features successfully clustered distinct pathological stages with the accuracy of 80.00 and 93.33%, respectively. The systematic framework, merging miniature programmable biochemical cascade pathways with multidimensional artificial intelligence predictions, provides a highly powerful novel diagnostic paradigm to overcome traditional barriers in complex liquid biopsy translational applications.

records.title: Tissue factor-specific sdAb radiotracers for molecular imaging in solid tumors.
records.abstract: Tissue factor (TF) expression has been associated with tumor aggressiveness and poor prognosis in several cancers. With the recent FDA approval of an antibody-drug-conjugate targeting TF, tisotumab vedotin for recurrent metastatic cervical cancer, companion diagnostic tools capable of capturing tumor heterogeneity are increasingly critical. In this study, we developed and characterized single domain antibody (sdAb)-based radiotracers to non-invasively visualize tumors expressing either murine (m) or human (h) TF protein. SdAbs targeting hTF and mTF were obtained from an immune llama library. Seven candidates targeting each species' orthologue were selected, characterized in vitro and radiolabeled with 99mTc for in vivo screening in athymic nude mice bearing both mTF and hTF positive tumors. Lead anti-hTF sdAb was radiolabeled with 68Ga for PET imaging. In vitro, all sdAbs exhibited excellent affinities for their respective targets, reaching the picomolar range. When radiolabeled with 99mTc, the lead compounds showed strong uptake and specific binding in TF-positive tumors as confirmed by SPECT imaging. The lead sdAb 64B4 targeting hTF protein, demonstrated an uptake of 8.07±1.02% IA/g in BxPC-3 tumors and a tumor-to-blood ratio of 26.06±4.36. The best candidate for targeting mTF protein, sdAb 66A12, displayed an uptake of 3.30±0.22% IA/g in mTF positive tumors and a tumor-to-blood ratio of 10.70±2.83. Off-tumor uptake was detected in several organs, with unexpectedly the highest levels detected in brown adipose tissue, consistent with mTF protein expression levels determined by ELISA. We successfully developed and validated sdAb-based radiotracers targeting either mTF or hTF, enabling the noninvasive visualization of TF-expressing tumors.

records.title: Label-free isolation of heterogeneous breast cancer cell populations via insulator-based dielectrophoresis.
records.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are valuable biomarkers for cancer diagnosis and monitoring, yet their isolation from blood remains challenging due to their phenotypic heterogeneity and rarity. Label-free microfluidic technologies offer a promising alternative to affinity-based approaches by exploiting intrinsic biophysical differences between cell types. Here, we developed a microfluidic platform for label-free cell separation based on insulator-based dielectrophoresis (iDEP). The microfluidic device employs an array of triangular insulating structures that generate strong electric field gradients in response to an externally applied alternating current (AC) electric field, enabling selective isolation of breast cancer cells from blood cells based on their dielectric properties. Hydrodynamic focusing is used to confine the sample stream and precisely control cell trajectories within the separation region. Numerical simulations were performed to optimize the electric field distribution and fluid flow characteristics within the device. Experimental validation using breast cancer cell lines (mesenchymal-like MDA-MB-231 cells and epithelial-like MCF-7 cells) spiked into peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) demonstrated selective dielectrophoretic deflection of cancer cells while PBMCs largely followed the central streamline. Approximately 98% of the cancer-cell flux detected across all outlets exited through the CTC outlets with a purity above 65% in 1 : 1 spike-in experiments. The ability to enrich both mesenchymal-like and epithelial-like breast cancer cells demonstrates the potential of the platform to address phenotypic heterogeneity which is a key challenge in label-free isolation of CTCs. The proposed system provides a simple label-free approach to separate heterogeneous cell populations and represents a promising tool for microfluidic liquid biopsy enrichment applications.

records.title: Pathobiology and Precision Management of Benign and Malignant Bone Tumors: A Narrative Review.
records.abstract: Bone tumors range from incidental benign lesions and locally aggressive intermediate tumors to primary sarcomas, and metastatic carcinoma is the most common malignant lesion of adult bone. This narrative review focuses on primary bone tumors, examining their classification, molecular pathobiology, diagnosis, staging, and treatment, and it addresses metastatic bone disease briefly from an orthopedic-oncology perspective. We synthesized literature identified through PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by targeted verification and updating of cited sources during revision in 2026. Classifications, clinical practice guidelines, clinical trials, cohort studies, and reviews informed the synthesis. Management depends on histological subtype, anatomical site, disease extent, symptoms, and the feasibility of preserving function. Suspected primary bone sarcomas should be imaged locally, staged with chest computed tomography, and referred to a sarcoma center before biopsy. Observation or intralesional treatment is appropriate for many benign lesions, whereas selected locally aggressive tumors require more extensive intervention. Osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma generally require systemic chemotherapy and local treatment. Surgery remains central to conventional chondrosarcoma management, and systemic treatment options differ across its subtypes. Molecular findings support, but do not replace, integrated radiological and histopathological diagnosis. Checkpoint inhibitors have shown limited activity in unselected bone sarcomas, and multikinase inhibitors have modest activity in relapsed osteosarcoma. Patient-specific implants, radiomics, liquid biopsy, and cellular therapies are promising, but each requires prospective evidence of improved patient outcomes before broad adoption. Accurate biopsy planning, specialist pathology review, and coordinated sarcoma care remain essential.

records.title: Circulating tumor DNA in Hodgkin lymphoma: biological classification, molecular residual disease, and integration with PET response.
records.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and its tumor-derived fraction, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), enable non-invasive tumor genotyping, longitudinal disease monitoring, and molecular residual disease (MRD) assessment. Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is particularly suitable for ctDNA-based analysis because malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells usually constitute only a small fraction of the tumor mass, whereas plasma may contain a strong tumor-derived DNA signal. This narrative review summarizes the potential applications of cfDNA-based ctDNA analysis in hematologic malignancies, with a focused emphasis on cHL. We discuss pre-analytical and analytical requirements, including plasma processing, tumor-informed and tumor-naive sequencing, error suppression, droplet digital PCR, and control for clonal hematopoiesis. We then synthesize evidence for ctDNA as a dual-readout biomarker: a baseline tool for non-invasive biological classification and a dynamic measure of molecular response. Published studies identify cHL genomic subtypes, associations with the tumor microenvironment, and prognostic information complementary to PET and conventional risk factors. Age-specific evidence is uneven, and most studies demonstrate analytical feasibility or prognosis rather than benefit from a ctDNA-triggered intervention. ctDNA-MRD should complement FDG-PET/CT; it cannot localize disease or currently replace established staging and response criteria. Routine implementation will require harmonized sample handling, validated assays and reporting thresholds, external quality assessment, and prospective trials demonstrating that ctDNA-guided treatment improves disease control, toxicity, or quality of life.

records.title: Diagnostic accuracy of liquid biopsy-based qPCR, ddPCR, and NGS in colorectal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.abstract: Detection of colorectal cancer (CRC) significantly improves survival, yet current screening methods face challenges regarding invasiveness and patient compliance. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a promising non-invasive alternative. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of liquid biopsy-based molecular diagnostics for colorectal cancer. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library for studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of molecular liquid biopsy for CRC. Using a bivariate random-effects model, we estimated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Meta-regression and subgroup analyses were performed to identify key drivers of performance, focusing on diagnostic platforms, biomarker types, and specimen sources. A total of 43 studies were included in the final analysis. The pooled sensitivity and specificity for liquid biopsy techniques (qPCR, ddPCR, and NGS) were 75% (95% CI, 0.70-0.79) and 91% (95% CI, 0.89-0.92), respectively. The SROC analysis revealed an AUC of 0.9121 (95% CI, 0.864-0.904). In subgroup analyses, NGS demonstrated a higher diagnostic odds ratio of 80.51 (95% CI, 26.13-248.08) and an AUC of 0.937. Furthermore, mutation-based biomarkers showed a diagnostic odds ratio of 45.78 (95% CI, 17.79-117.8) with an AUC of 0.944, while plasma samples had a diagnostic odds ratio of 32.19 (95% CI, 21.02-49.29) and an AUC of 0.912, indicating relatively higher diagnostic accuracy. Subgroup observations suggest that plasma-based mutation analysis using NGS exhibits promising diagnostic accuracy for CRC. Overall, these findings indicate that molecular liquid biopsy may serve as a potential non-invasive adjunct to complement traditional screening strategies, though further validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.
